[2025-03-30 12:09] nicmo7829 : KOB is a football manager game where you are both the manager and the club owner. Not only do you have to manage the players and tactics, but you also need to handle the financial aspect. If you want to blindly upgrade your players indefinitely, you have to pay for it by contributing more to the league prize.  I'm not supposed to teach you how to play the game, but... If you're worried about the financial side—which is completely understandable—you need to evaluate your competition in your league. Decide how far you're willing to stretch the wages that come with your squad getting better and better. If you think you're overpaying compared to other managers in your league, then hold off on upgrading your players' AVQ skills and focus on free skills instead. This way, other clubs can catch up, raising their wages and, in turn, increasing the league bonus. Once this happens, you'll see that the league prize makes it worthwhile for you to push a little further, and so on.
[2025-03-30 12:10] nicmo7829 : Stopping wages in protest will only make things worse for everyone, especially for you. You'll lose matches, and next season's league prizes will be smaller. 100% of player wages go back to the clubs. If you think the proportion is wrong and you want to win more than you pay, it's because you're too far ahead. If all it took was injecting money and not worrying about management, then everyone would be profitable.  PSG has the highest wages, it's also 1st in the ELO ranking—basically the best team in the game. They are statistically the hardest to beat. If you're looking for a scenario where you just put in money and make a guaranteed profit, there are other products out there. Check your banking app—plenty of options there. In KOB, there is real competition between many users trying to beat you with their strategies. Anyway, I am always open to suggestions that make any aspects of the game better. Complaining and not having a suggestion of a possible change is not really a suggestion, its a complaint where you didn't care to spend time thinking how it works and how it could be better.

[2025-07-26 20:34] nicmo7829 : The process is a seeded draw that uses a pot system based on team ELO ratings to ensure a balanced distribution. It also includes randomization and a critical constraint to prevent teams from the same country from being in the same group.  Here is a step-by-step breakdown of the logic:  Team Selection: Initially, teams are selected from different leagues based on the number of available spots for each country.  ELO-Based Sorting (Seeding): All the selected teams are then sorted in descending order based on their elo rating. This is the most important step for seeding, as it places the highest-rated teams at the top of the list and the lowest-rated at the bottom.  Pot Creation: The sorted list of teams is divided into batches (or "pots"). The size of each batch is equal to the number of groups. For example, if there are 32 teams and 8 groups, the teams are split into four pots of eight teams each: Pot 1: The 8 teams with the highest ELO ratings. Pot 2: The next 8 teams by ELO rating. Pot 3: The next 8 teams. Pot 4: The 8 teams with the lowest ELO ratings.  Randomized Group Draw: The system then draws one team from each pot for each group. It does this by: Shuffling the teams within each pot to randomize the draw. Assigning one team from the shuffled pot to each of the available groups.  Country Constraint: A crucial rule is enforced during the draw: no two teams from the same country can be placed in the same group.  Validation and Retries: After an initial attempt to create the groups, the system validates them against the country constraint. If any group violates this rule, the entire draw is discarded, and the shuffling and distribution process is repeated. This continues until a valid set of groups is formed.
[2025-07-27 05:00] ralf00048 : So is like the old UCL system in RL
[2025-07-27 05:01] ralf00048 : Four groups divided by elo and a draw from each pot for each group with the restriction of country
[2025-07-27 05:01] ralf00048 : Just like the old sistem in real life

[2026-10-21 07:41] siralex90 : Since October 17th, I’ve only played one friendly match with my Swiss national team, why is that? What does it depend on? Sometimes these matches happen every day, while at other times they’re quite rare.. they should be made available daily, otherwise, it’s really difficult to climb the elo rankings.
[2026-10-21 08:39] nicmo7829 : Once a day at midnight server time, the game takes the 20 national teams that have gone longest without a match. It pairs them at random into 10 friendlies, all kicking off at 20:00 that day. There are 53 playable national teams, so each one gets a friendly about every 2.65 days. During the World Cup (Oct 1–19), the teams still in it were left out of the draw. Only about 21 teams were left for 20 places, so Switzerland, which wasn't in the World Cup, played every day from Oct 1 to 6. As teams were knocked out they rejoined, and the gap grew to every other day (Oct 8, 10, 12, 14, 16).

[2024-12-29 13:09] maridiba : I agree with <@648913184228376617>. Players' ratings in matches are not reliable enough to serve as a key factor for confidence, as they are based on an "additive system". The more good actions a player performs, the higher their rating, without accounting for how many duels they lose. For example, if a goalkeeper saves 2 shots out of 10, they would receive a better rating than one who saves the only shot their team concedes.  I would suggest using a different indicator, perhaps a success rate (duels won/total duels), to influence confidence. Even without differentiating between duel types (offensive or defensive, buildup or shots, etc.), it would still be more reliable than match ratings

[2025-07-05 13:04] maridiba : This has nothing in common with KOB economy. In that case, there are people funding the business (the ones who buy food) and people earning and sharing that money (stores, banks, agricultural suppliers, farmers...). That's more similar to real football, in which you have players and agents milking the clubs, clubs milking sponsors and fans, and the sponsors milking the fans. Summarizing, everybody is milking the fans, who are the ones funding the business.  In KOB you don't have football players who earn money or fans funding the business, it's the same money running in circles, as expected in a zero-sum game. The ones funding the economy are the same who earn from it, the users. One can still make profit from the game, but it means someone else has to lose money because, on average, the funds are balanced. And the same applies to players market.

[2026-05-30 09:19] chantilax : Youth Players problem from Certain Countries  I've noticed that when buying youth players, it's practically impossible to see their attributes (AVQ) in some countries. They almost never reach level 6, which is where the AVQ is displayed and gives an idea of ​​the player's skill level before signing them.  Countries like Spain, Poland, Romania, Italy, the Netherlands...  What might happen in the future? There won't be good players from these countries because they're mostly bought with 1* and completely blindly (before level 6). So, in, say, six seasons, the current national team starters will retire, and the managers who take over the national team won't have good players to call up.  In my case, being Spanish, I'd like to take care of Spanish youth players and, when signing prospects, make sure they're Spanish, but unfortunately, we can't.  This could be a problem in the short or medium term and seriously hurt the countries with the most managers in the game. I've also noticed that less experienced managers tend to buy youth players from their own country by default. That is, a Polish manager will buy Polish youth players, so if there are many Polish managers and their youth players are bought with one star rating, there won't be a good Polish national team in the future.  We need to think about how to protect against this somehow.  Regards, Chantilax

[2026-09-21 13:09] maridiba : There is already a difference between the formation. This is in the documentation:  Formations There are several formations to choose from, 4-4-2 being the default and most neutral formation. Any other formation may bring bonuses or penalties to a determined play. For example, a defending team using 5-3-2 will see a benefit when one of the 5 defenders is going for a tackle. However if the same team is defending using 3-4-3, the same defender will be less effective as they are missing 1 player. The same is true if the player defending is a midfielder or striker, the match engine will also check how many players there are in that position. Same logic when attacking, a lone striker in a 4-5-1 will struggle to score, comparing to 3-4-3 but since his midfield has 5 players, he will probably be served more often.  So, we can assume that in KOB, 5-3-2 is a defensive formation, 3-4-3 is an attacking formation that will be weaker defending but every attack using a striker, is stronger. This logic is the same for all formations.  For every official match a team plays with a formation, it will gain a 1 star experience towards that formation knowledge, each star gained gives a 1% bonus to players skills for the next match. This experience can be accumulated up to 5 stars, giving a maximum of 5% bonus. To stack this experience the game will only look for the latest 15 official matches, older than that, they will be "forgotten". Formation experience will give bonus to every match type however can only be accumulated on official matches. Formation experience is reset at the end of each season.

[2026-09-21 14:14] 9jathug : It's not as simple as one defender is missing in 352 so it's less defensive than 442 or that any formation with 4 line up would be better in defence than formation with 3 defense line up.  Tactical instruction can upset and switch line of priorities in which a defensive line up of 4 men become more vulnerable than 3 defender formation.  Aside those simple it's three men it's less defensive or it's 4 men it will be more defensive, there are more to it. The philosophy behind that of 422 against 352 is way more complex than you simplified into 3 or 4 men. The direction and role of player on the pitch base on formation is the key.  In simple explanation, some formation is just vulnerable against another formation and vice verser. The only easy way you can implement that on football manager game simulation would be give formation some benefit in form of bonus 5% when playing against another formation it's mostly consider by football analysts as been better than.  That 5% or whatever bonus added doesn't automatically mean 352 would win against 442. If 442 team players are way more stronger then 352 team players, the probability would still be in the favour of the better squad.  But in a close match with clubs that have similar strengths, there  formation  advantages against another formation become a thing for manager to exploit.   Not just randomly trying to play 4 men defense against 3 men hoping somehow playing attack on 442 against 352 gives you better chance in attack while maintaining good defensive line up of 4 men. Doesn't work that way
